title: Fossils
examples: How long ago did dinosaurs live?
What is the difference between a fossil and a bone?

explain.say: Today we are learning about fossils. Fossils are remains of ancient life. They help us learn about the past.
Fossils form when living things get covered by sediment. This sediment protects them from being eaten. Over a long time, this process happens.
Sometimes the hard parts of the creature remain. Minerals can replace the original material slowly. This process keeps the shape safe.
Fossils tell scientists about past environments. They show us what animals and plants lived near us. They help build a picture of history.
Trace fossils are evidence of life, not the life itself. They show things like footprints or burrows. These marks tell us how creatures moved.
In real life, finding a fossil helps us understand climate change. We can see what plants lived when the world was much warmer.

faq.q: How long does it take for a fossil to form?
faq.a: It takes a very, very long time to form a fossil. This process can take millions of years to complete.
asks: How many years does it take?

faq.a: No, fossils can be many things. They can be imprints, tracks, or even shells. They are evidence of life.

faq.q: What is the difference between a fossil and a modern bone?
faq.a: A fossil has been changed by minerals over deep time. A modern bone is from a creature that lived recently.
asks: How do I tell if it is old?

faq.a: Trace fossils are signs of life, like footprints or tunnels. They show us what an animal did, not what it was.

faq.q: Where do we find the best fossils?
faq.a: We often find fossils in sedimentary rock layers. These layers build up over vast periods of time.
asks: What kind of rock holds fossils?
Where do scientists look for fossils?

facts: Fossils are preserved remains of ancient organisms.
The process of fossilization requires sediment to cover the remains.
Trace fossils show evidence of activity, like tracks or nests.
Fossils help scientists understand past environments and climates.

quiz.say: What is the best word to describe the remains of an ancient animal?
quiz.why: A fossil is the correct term for preserved ancient life.

wrong.0: A skeleton is only the hard bones of a creature.
wrong.1: Sediment is what covers the remains, not the remains themselves.
wrong.2: A trace is only evidence of movement, not the actual body.

quiz.say: If you find a dinosaur footprint in rock, what kind of fossil is it?
quiz.why: Footprints are signs of movement, making them trace fossils.

wrong.0: This describes how it formed, not what it is.
wrong.1: The rock layer is the material containing the fossil.
wrong.3: A body fossil must be the actual remains of the creature.

quiz.say: What process helps preserve the original life form over time?
quiz.why: Mineralization is the process where minerals replace the original material.

wrong.1: Decomposition is the process that usually destroys life.
wrong.2: Burial is the covering, but mineralization is the preservation step.
wrong.3: Erosion is the wearing away of rock, which removes fossils.
